dataset.name: Olist Brazilian E-Commerce
dataset.description: Public dataset of transactions from Olist, a Brazilian e-commerce platform. Contains order, item, payment, review, customer, product, and seller data spanning September 2016 to October 2018.

olist_orders_dataset.purpose: Core order records, one row per order placed by a customer.

grain.description: One row represents a single order from a customer, with timestamps and delivery status.

customer_id.semantics: Foreign key to the customer who placed the order. Use this to join orders → customers. For 'unique customers', use customer_unique_id instead.
customer_id.gotchas: Two customer ID columns exist: customer_id (order-level identifier, 99,441 distinct) and customer_unique_id (person-level, 96,096 distinct). Use customer_id for joins; use customer_unique_id to count unique people or identify repeat buyers.

order_status.semantics: Status of the order (8 values: delivered, shipped, canceled, unavailable, invoiced, processing, created, approved).
order_status.gotchas: Revenue questions must pick a convention: booked revenue excludes only 'canceled' and 'unavailable'; realized revenue includes only 'delivered'. Default to booked unless question explicitly references delivery/shipping/fulfillment.

order_purchase_timestamp.semantics: Date and time when the customer placed the order.

order_approved_at.semantics: Date and time when the order was approved (payment confirmed).

order_delivered_carrier_date.semantics: Date and time when the carrier picked up the order from the seller.

order_delivered_customer_date.semantics: Date and time when the customer received the order.
order_delivered_customer_date.null_rate_note: NULL for ~3% of orders; always NULL unless order_status = 'delivered'.
order_delivered_customer_date.gotchas: Use this column for delivery-performance questions, filtering to order_status = 'delivered' and non-null values.

order_estimated_delivery_date.semantics: Promised delivery date (set at order time).

common_joins.note: Get items, product details, seller info for the order
Get customer review and rating for the order

aggregation_notes: Sum order-level metrics (order_value, etc.) without grouping; each order_id appears once.
To count orders by status, use COUNT(*) GROUP BY order_status (will not double-count).
typical_questions: How many orders in a time period?
What is the order status distribution?
What is the on-time delivery rate?
How long does delivery take?

olist_order_items_dataset.purpose: Line items (products) within each order, with price and freight.

grain.description: One row represents a single line item (product SKU) within an order. An order may have multiple rows.

order_item_id.semantics: Sequence number of this line item within the order (1, 2, 3, ...). NOT a quantity column.
order_item_id.gotchas: order_item_id is a line-item sequence counter, NOT quantity. SUM(price * order_item_id) is a bug. Correct revenue per order is SUM(price) GROUP BY order_id.

seller_id.semantics: Foreign key to the seller who supplied this item.

shipping_limit_date.semantics: Deadline for the seller to ship the item.

price.semantics: Unit price of the product (merchandise only, excludes freight).

freight_value.semantics: Shipping cost for this line item.
freight_value.gotchas: freight_value is stored here, NOT in payments. Total billed per order = SUM(order_items.price) + SUM(order_items.freight_value). This will differ from SUM(payments.payment_value) by ~0.02% due to rounding on installments/vouchers.

common_joins.note: Get product name, category, and dimensions
Get English translation of Portuguese product category
Get order status and delivery dates

aggregation_notes: Merchandise revenue = SUM(price) GROUP BY order_id or by time period.
Total revenue with freight = SUM(price) + SUM(freight_value) GROUP BY order_id.
Average item price = SUM(price) / COUNT(*) or AVG(price) (valid both ways).
Revenue by product = SUM(price) GROUP BY product_id.
Revenue by seller = SUM(price) GROUP BY seller_id.
typical_questions: What is the total revenue per order?
What products are best sellers?
What is the average order size (items per order)?
Which sellers have the most revenue?
What is the average freight cost?

olist_order_payments_dataset.purpose: Payment records for orders, one or more rows per order depending on method and installments.

grain.description: One row represents a single payment row for an order. Orders may have 1+ rows (installments, mixed payment methods, or both).

payment_sequential.semantics: Sequence number of this payment within the order (1, 2, ...). Not all orders have multiple payments.

payment_type.semantics: Method of payment (5 values: credit_card, boleto, voucher, debit_card, not_defined).
payment_type.gotchas: payment_type has 5 values including 'not_defined' (3 rows with payment_value = $0.00). Filter out 'not_defined' for any revenue or payment-count question.

payment_installments.semantics: Number of installments for this payment (1 = full, >1 = split across N months).

payment_value.semantics: Amount paid in this payment row. Includes freight and merchandise.
payment_value.gotchas: payment_value INCLUDES freight. order_items.price does NOT. SUM(payment_value) = total paid across all payment rows in an order. SUM(order_items.price) + SUM(order_items.freight_value) = total billed. These differ by ~0.02% due to voucher/installment rounding, not an error.

aggregation_notes: Total revenue paid = SUM(payment_value) GROUP BY order_id (or unfiltered for dataset total).
Do NOT group by payment_type then sum; an order with mixed methods will be double-counted.
To find orders using each method: COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) GROUP BY payment_type (counts orders, not payment rows).
For installment analysis: COUNT(*) GROUP BY payment_installments gives payment-row counts; divide by installment count to get order count.
typical_questions: What is total revenue?
What payment methods are used?
What fraction of orders use installments?
How many installments do customers choose on average?

olist_order_reviews_dataset.purpose: Customer reviews and satisfaction ratings for orders.

grain.description: One row represents a review (potentially from a repeat reviewer) for a specific order. Composite key on (review_id, order_id).

review_id.semantics: Identifier for the review. NOT unique on its own; one reviewer can submit the same review_id for multiple orders.
review_id.gotchas: review_id is NOT unique by itself. Composite primary key is (review_id, order_id). Do NOT use review_id alone to deduplicate.

order_id.semantics: Foreign key to the order being reviewed.

review_score.gotchas: Distribution is heavily skewed: ~57.8% of reviews are 5-star. AVG(review_score) is almost always ~4.0–4.1 and rarely informative. Prefer reporting the full distribution or the fraction of 1–2 scores ('detractors') for satisfaction analysis.

review_comment_title.semantics: Short text title/headline of the review.

review_comment_message.semantics: Full text message of the review.

review_creation_date.semantics: Date and time when the customer submitted the review.

review_answer_timestamp.semantics: Date and time when the seller responded to the review.

common_joins.note: Get order status and delivery dates

aggregation_notes: Average review score = AVG(review_score). Note: heavily skewed to 5-star; distributions are more informative.
Count of reviews = COUNT(*). Most orders have a review; some do not.
Distribution of scores = COUNT(*) GROUP BY review_score.
Detractor rate = COUNT(*) FILTER (review_score IN (1, 2)) / COUNT(*) * 100.
typical_questions: What is the average review score?
What is the distribution of star ratings?
What fraction of reviews are 1 or 2 stars?
Do delivered orders have higher ratings than shipped orders?

olist_customers_dataset.purpose: Customer master data including location and identifier mapping.

grain.description: One row per order placed (customer_id is order-level). Multiple rows can share the same customer_unique_id (repeat customers).

customer_id.semantics: Unique identifier per order. Use this to join orders → customers.
customer_id.gotchas: customer_id is 1:1 with orders (99,441 distinct). Do NOT use it to count unique customers; use customer_unique_id instead.

customer_unique_id.semantics: Unique identifier per person (96,096 distinct). Use this to identify repeat customers or count unique people.
customer_unique_id.gotchas: This is the person-level ID. customer_unique_id is many-to-one with customer_id. Use COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) for 'unique customers', NOT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id).

customer_zip_code_prefix.semantics: Prefix of the customer's postal code.
customer_zip_code_prefix.gotchas: Partial zip code (prefix only), not full postal code. No latitude/longitude.

customer_city.semantics: City name (in Portuguese) where the customer is located.
customer_city.gotchas: Geographic fields are strings only; no coordinates or distance calculations possible without the missing geolocation table.

customer_state.semantics: State abbreviation (e.g., 'SP', 'RJ') where the customer is located.

common_joins.note: Get customer details for every order

aggregation_notes: To count unique customers = COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id), NOT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id).
Orders per unique customer = COUNT(*) GROUP BY customer_unique_id / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id).
Repeat customer rate = (COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) with >1 order) / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id).
typical_questions: How many unique customers?
What fraction of customers are repeat buyers?
Which states have the most customers?
What is the average orders per customer?

olist_products_dataset.purpose: Product master data including category, name length, description, photos, and physical dimensions.

grain.description: One row per unique product (SKU). Physical attributes and category are static.

product_category_name.semantics: Category name in Portuguese. Join to product_category_name_translation for English.
product_category_name.gotchas: product_category_name is in Portuguese. 610 products (~1.8%) have NULL category. Two categories have NO English translation: 'pc_gamer' (3 products) and 'portateis_cozinha_e_preparadores_de_alimentos' (10 products). Always join to product_category_name_translation for English; filter NULLs if needed.

product_name_lenght.semantics: Character count of the product name (note: column name has typo 'lenght').

product_description_lenght.semantics: Character count of the product description (note: column name has typo 'lenght').

product_photos_qty.semantics: Number of product photos in the listing.

common_joins.note: Get sales and revenue per product

aggregation_notes: Revenue per product = SUM(order_items.price) GROUP BY product_id.
Best-selling products = COUNT(*) GROUP BY product_id ORDER BY COUNT DESC.
Average product weight/dimensions = AVG(product_weight_g), etc.
typical_questions: Which products are best sellers by revenue or volume?
What is the average product weight or size?
Which categories are most popular?
How do products with more photos perform?

olist_sellers_dataset.purpose: Seller master data including geographic location.

grain.description: One row per seller (vendor). Static location data.

seller_zip_code_prefix.semantics: Prefix of the seller's postal code.
seller_zip_code_prefix.gotchas: Partial zip code (prefix only), not full postal code. No latitude/longitude.

seller_city.semantics: City name (in Portuguese) where the seller is located.
seller_city.gotchas: Geographic fields are strings only; no coordinates or distance calculations possible without the missing geolocation table.

seller_state.semantics: State abbreviation (e.g., 'SP', 'RJ') where the seller is located.

common_joins.note: Get sales and revenue per seller

aggregation_notes: Revenue per seller = SUM(order_items.price) GROUP BY seller_id.
Items sold per seller = COUNT(*) GROUP BY seller_id.
Seller count = COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id).
typical_questions: Which sellers have the most revenue?
How many sellers are there?
Which states have the most sellers?
What is the average order volume per seller?

product_category_name_translation.purpose: Mapping of Portuguese product category names to English translations.

grain.description: One row per product category in the Portuguese dataset, with English translation (if available).

product_category_name_english.semantics: English translation of the category name.
product_category_name_english.null_rate_note: Two Portuguese categories have NO English translation: 'pc_gamer' and 'portateis_cozinha_e_preparadores_de_alimentos'.
product_category_name_english.gotchas: Two categories lack translations. If your analysis requires English names, filter WHERE product_category_name_english IS NOT NULL, or handle the NULL cases separately.

common_joins.note: Get English category names for reporting

aggregation_notes: This is a reference table; aggregation is rare. Use it to translate category names before grouping.
typical_questions: What is the English name for a Portuguese category?

cardinalities.customer_id_to_orders: one-to-one (customer_id is order-level; 99,441 distinct vs 99,441 orders)
cardinalities.customer_unique_id_to_customer_id: one-to-many (one person can place multiple orders)

revenue.description: Total monetary value of orders, with multiple valid definitions depending on what you measure.

definitions.name: revenue_from_payments
definitions.sql_sketch: SELECT SUM(olist_order_payments_dataset.payment_value) FROM olist_order_payments_dataset WHERE olist_order_payments_dataset.payment_type <> 'not_defined' GROUP BY ... (or unfiltered for dataset total)
definitions.use_when: You want total cash received (includes freight, installment-adjusted). Use for cash flow and payment reconciliation. Filter payment_type <> 'not_defined' to exclude 3 zero-value placeholder rows.

definitions.name: revenue_from_items_and_freight
definitions.sql_sketch: SELECT SUM(olist_order_items_dataset.price) + SUM(olist_order_items_dataset.freight_value) FROM olist_order_items_dataset GROUP BY ... (or unfiltered for dataset total)
definitions.use_when: You want total billed to customers (merchandise + shipping). Use for sales and revenue recognition. Differs from payment_value by ~0.02% due to voucher/installment rounding (not an error).

definitions.name: merchandise_revenue
definitions.sql_sketch: SELECT SUM(olist_order_items_dataset.price) FROM olist_order_items_dataset GROUP BY ... (or unfiltered for dataset total)
definitions.use_when: You want revenue excluding freight. Use for product-level or category-level analysis where shipping is not relevant.

revenue.expected_delta: ~0.02% between payment-based and item-based revenue due to rounding on installments and vouchers. Deltas >0.5% indicate a data quality issue.

unique_customers.description: Count of distinct individuals (people) who made purchases, identified by customer_unique_id.

definitions.name: unique_customers_correct
definitions.use_when: Always. This is the person-level unique count (96,096 total).

definitions.name: unique_customers_wrong_pattern
definitions.use_when: NEVER. This returns the count of orders (99,441), not unique people, because customer_id is order-level.

unique_customers.expected_delta: There is no delta; use only the first definition. The second is a common mistake.

avg_delivery_days.description: Average number of days from order placement to customer delivery, for delivered orders only.

definitions.name: avg_delivery_days_delivered_only
definitions.sql_sketch: SELECT AVG(EXTRACT(DAY FROM (olist_orders_dataset.order_delivered_customer_date - olist_orders_dataset.order_purchase_timestamp))) FROM olist_orders_dataset WHERE olist_orders_dataset.order_status = 'delivered' AND olist_orders_dataset.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
definitions.use_when: Always use this for delivery time analysis. Filter to order_status = 'delivered' and non-null delivered_customer_date to avoid ~3% of orders with NULL delivery date.

on_time_delivery_rate.description: Fraction of delivered orders that arrived on or before the estimated delivery date.

definitions.name: on_time_delivery_rate
definitions.sql_sketch: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (olist_orders_dataset.order_delivered_customer_date <= olist_orders_dataset.order_estimated_delivery_date) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) FROM olist_orders_dataset WHERE olist_orders_dataset.order_status = 'delivered' AND olist_orders_dataset.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
definitions.use_when: Always. Filter to delivered orders with non-null delivery date. Result is a percentage (0–100).

repeat_customer_rate.description: Fraction of unique customers who placed more than one order.

definitions.name: repeat_customer_rate
definitions.sql_sketch: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN customer_order_count > 1 THEN customer_unique_id END) * 100.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) FROM (SELECT olist_customers_dataset.customer_unique_id, COUNT(*) as customer_order_count FROM olist_customers_dataset GROUP BY customer_unique_id)
definitions.use_when: To measure loyalty and repeat-purchase behavior.

average_order_value.description: Mean monetary value per order (total paid or total billed, depending on choice).

definitions.name: aov_from_payments
definitions.sql_sketch: SELECT SUM(olist_order_payments_dataset.payment_value) / COUNT(DISTINCT olist_order_payments_dataset.order_id) FROM olist_order_payments_dataset WHERE olist_order_payments_dataset.payment_type <> 'not_defined'

definitions.name: aov_from_items
definitions.use_when: Billing-focused; includes freight. Slightly differs from payment-based due to rounding (~0.02%).

cross_table_gotchas: order_items and order_payments both contribute to order value but store it differently. order_items.price excludes freight; order_payments.payment_value includes it. order_items.freight_value holds shipping separately. Computing total revenue two ways will legitimately differ by ~0.02% (voucher/installment rounding), not by the full freight amount.
order_status is in orders; reviews exist even for non-delivered orders (some shipped/canceled orders have reviews). Do not assume reviews only exist for delivered orders.

customers has TWO id columns: customer_id (order-level, 1:1 with orders) and customer_unique_id (person-level, 96,096 distinct). Mixing them causes cardinality errors. Use customer_id to join orders; use customer_unique_id to count unique people.

order_items can have multiple rows per order (order_item_id = 1, 2, 3, ...). Summing without grouping will create a Cartesian product if you join to other many-to-one tables without GROUP BY. Always GROUP BY order_id before aggregating order-level metrics.

order_payments can have multiple rows per order (installments and/or mixed payment methods). Summing payment_value across the table is correct; grouping by payment_type then summing will double-count orders with mixed methods.
reviews (order_reviews_dataset) has a composite key (review_id, order_id). review_id alone is NOT unique. One reviewer can leave the same review on multiple orders.

Three distinct date fields in orders: order_purchase_timestamp (always present), order_delivered_customer_date (NULL for ~3%; NULL whenever status <> 'delivered'), order_estimated_delivery_date (always present). Use the right one for your analysis.
unanswerable_question_hints: Time coverage is 2016-09-04 through 2018-10-17. Questions about Q1/Q2/Q3 2016 or post-October 2018 are unanswerable.
No cost of goods sold (COGS), marketing spend, salaries, or overhead. Profit, margin, CAC, LTV, ROI, break-even, and unit economics are unanswerable.
No returns or refunds data. Return rates, returned revenue, refund volume, and return reasons are unanswerable.
No inventory data. Stock levels, stockouts, backorders, and carrying cost are unanswerable.

Geolocation table (olist_geolocation_dataset) is NOT present by design. Distance calculations, maps, city/state geometry, and any lat/long reasoning are unanswerable. Only string city/state fields are available (customer_city, customer_state, seller_city, seller_state).
No order-modification data. Questions about cancellations by reason, refund amounts, returns by defect, or customer service interactions beyond seller responses to reviews are unanswerable.
